disclaimer: Policy language paraphrased from publisher help centers. No performance metrics.

facts.title: Policy coverage areas
facts.claim: Google Ads policies cover four broad areas: prohibited content, prohibited practices, restricted content and features, and editorial and technical quality standards.

facts.title: Dangerous products or services
facts.claim: Google does not allow promotion of some products or services that cause damage, harm, or injury, including recreational drugs, weapons, ammunition, explosives, and tobacco products (non-exhaustive examples in the help article).

facts.title: Inappropriate or offensive content
facts.claim: Ads or destinations that display shocking content or promote hatred, intolerance, discrimination, or violence are not allowed.

facts.title: Official policy language
facts.claim: Google states that the English version of the Advertising Policies Help Center is the official language used to enforce Google Ads policies.

facts.title: Limited Ad Serving update (August 2026)
facts.claim: In August 2026 Google updated Limited Ad Serving to cover all Google Ads; ads from unqualified advertisers may have impressions limited in scenarios more likely to produce negative ads experiences.

facts.title: Age-estimation restricted categories (June 2026)
facts.claim: While Google is estimating a user's age, it continues to restrict adult content and pornography, alcohol, and gambling. The former Default Ads Treatment policy was renamed to describe this interim protection.

facts.title: Dangerous products pilot (October 2026)
facts.claim: Google announced a limited six-month United States pilot beginning October 2026 to allow ads for certain gun accessories (examples listed: bipods, sights, slings, mounts, and braces) on Search only; ads for firearms, ammunition, and regulated parts remain prohibited, and the pilot does not apply outside the United States or on other surfaces.

facts.title: Prohibited Commercial Practices
facts.claim: Meta prohibits content and ads that use deceptive commercial practices to mislead people out of money, property, or personal information, including false job or government-program offers, celebrity/brand bait, guaranteed-return investment schemes, debt-relief and credit-repair schemes, get-rich-quick and giveaway schemes, romance schemes, and charity schemes.

facts.title: Ads must follow PCP community standard
facts.claim: Meta Advertising Standards require ads to comply with the Community Standard on Prohibited Commercial Practices.

facts.title: Adult nudity and sexual activity in ads
facts.claim: Meta ads must not contain imagery depicting nudity, sexual activity, people in explicit or sexually suggestive positions, or sexually suggestive activities; additional 18+ targeting applies to specified health or body-focused imagery.

facts.title: Health and wellness age restriction
facts.claim: Meta restricts advertising that promotes weight-loss or weight-gain products, cosmetic procedures, and dietary or health supplements from targeting users under 18, and bans specified incurable-disease cure claims.
